title: VPC On‑Prem Upgrade & Terraform Module Migration Tactics
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a tactical playbook for upgrading Private deployments (VPC and onprem) where we need to: (1) migrate/refactor Terraform modules, (2) upgrade serving runtime and control plane components, (3) validate API compatibility, and (4) define safe rollback sequences. The audience is platform engineers and solutions engineers owning customer onprem upgrades.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to releases v2.x -> v3.0 of the private-control-plane and serving-runtime images.
- Customers run the private control plane in a VPC or air-gapped onprem cluster using our Terraform modules (legacy tf-mod-legacy/*).
- State backend may be S3+DynamoDB lock, GCS, or local remote state used by partner installers — playbook includes migration notes.
- We assume CI pipeline can build and publish new runtime images to an internal registry accessible from customer env (or customer mirrors images).

High-level strategy:
1) Prepare Terraform module migration in a canary environment (internal lab cluster mimicking customer topology).
2) Run module refactor to new module namespace (tf-mod-v3/*) without changing infra semantics where possible. Use feature flags for new behaviors.
3) Deploy control plane v3 in parallel (side-by-side) where supported; otherwise use rolling in-place upgrade with blue-green pattern at the service level.
4) Upgrade serving runtime with staged rollout: worker pools first (low-traffic), then control plane components.
5) Run API/contract tests, smoke tests, and perf microbenchmarks.
6) Observe metrics for 1–2 business days (or customer SLA window) before full cutover.

Terraform module migration notes (practical tactics):
- Keep the migration backward compatible: new modules should accept legacy variable names via input aliases to avoid upstream changes.
- Add a migration guide script: scripts/tfstate-migrate.sh that does the following: terraform state pull -> sed transform to rename module path -> terraform state push (behind a lock). Test this in lab.
- Use a read-only dry-run workspace using TF_PLAN only and produce a canonical plan file archived with CI. Avoid auto-apply on first pass.
- Remote state lock: ensure at least one lock provider (DynamoDB for AWS S3 backends or GCS locks). Document manual lock/unlock steps if local state must be converted.
- Module versioning: publish v3 modules under registry path modules/private/v3 and pin them in customer manifests. Provide a compatibility matrix mapping old resources -> new resource names.
- Sensitive resource renaming: avoid renaming stateful resources (RDS, internal DB clusters, persistent volumes). If unavoidable, include explicit terraform state mv examples.

Control plane upgrade choreography:
- Goal: minimal downtime, maintain API compatibility for admin APIs, and preserve in-flight operations.
- Pattern A (preferred): side-by-side control plane in same VPC with route-level switch. Steps:
  * Deploy v3 control plane into new ASG/nodepool with same DB instance (read-write).
  * Run schema migration in transactional mode with backward-compatible changes; use dual-write pattern where necessary.
  * Switch traffic at the LB or API gateway level to new control plane once health checks pass.
- Pattern B (fallback): rolling in-place upgrade where side-by-side isn't possible:
  * Pre-warm nodes with new image and ensure they join cluster but remain drained.
  * Drain a node, upgrade, run smoke tests, then uncordon. Proceed one node at a time.

Database and schema migrations:
- Never run destructive schema migrations during first deploy. Use additive migrations with feature toggles.
- Provide a migration-runbook with commands for offline migrations: db-migrate status; db-migrate up --step=1; rollback: db-migrate down --step=1.
- Back up DB snapshot before applying any migrations. Store snapshot identifier in release notes.

Serving runtime upgrade and KV cache handling:
- Runtime includes KV cache and prefix-cache. Plan for cache warmup: after new workers start, prefetch hot prefixes from existing cache or run a warmup job that replays a small sample of production traces (anonymized).
- Strategy: bring up small new-worker pool with image v3 and join dispatcher, but mark it low-weight for routing. Gradually increase weight while observing tail latency and error rates.
- If model binary format (quantization/layout) changes, include model conversion tools in migration image and keep previous model variants available for fallback.

API compatibility checklist (admin + runtime APIs):
- Validate all API endpoints used by customer orchestration: /v1/models, /v1/predict, /admin/metrics, /admin/health.
- Backwards compatibility tests: run a suite that replays API calls captured in last 30 days (anonymized) against v3 in lab.
- Document breaking changes explicitly and provide compatibility shims where feasible (e.g., header name mapping, deprecation headers).

Testing matrix (minimum):
- Unit/Integration: terraform plan/apply in lab; module-level unit tests using kitchen-terraform.
- Contract tests: API replay against v3 control plane and runtime.
- Load test: 10–20% of peak traffic in lab with same latency SLOs.
- Canaries: run 1–3 customer canaries with opt-in.

Observability and KPIs to watch during rollout:
- 50th/95th/99th token latency for generation requests.
- Error rate (5xx, 4xx), RPC timeouts.
- Control plane API error rates and reconciliation loop duration.
- Cost signal: GPU utilization and average tokens/sec per worker.
- Terraform drift alerts: unexpected resource changes post-apply.

Rollback plan (explicit sequences):
- Rollback window: keep rollback procedure ready for first 24–48 hours.
- Control plane rollback:
  * If side-by-side: switch LB back to v2 routing, scale down v3, investigate DB state.
  * If rolling: roll nodes back following the inverse node sequence; rely on image tags (immutable) to avoid re-pulling previous images accidentally.
- Runtime rollback:
  * Drain new-worker pool, bring back old image worker pool, restore model symlinks if model format changed.
  * If model conversion was applied in-place to shared storage, restore from snapshot.
- Terraform rollback: restore remote state snapshot taken before module change and re-apply legacy module versions. Keep TF plan artifacts to speed this.

Risk register (top items):
- DB schema drift causing subtle runtime errors -> mitigated by dual-write and canary migrations.
- Remote state conflicts during migration -> mitigate with detailed lock steps and a single operator.
- Model binary incompatibility -> mitigate with conversion tooling and keep old variant available.
- Networking differences in customer VPCs causing side-by-side failure -> mitigate by pre-validating CIDR, security groups, and NAT/proxy configs.

Runbook checklist (operator quick steps):
1) Pre-upgrade: take TF remote-state backup, DB snapshot, publish release notes to customer, schedule maintenance window.
2) Apply Terraform in lab using tf-mod-v3, inspect plan; run state migration script in dry-run.
3) Deploy control plane v3 in lab and run contract tests.
4) Mirror steps in customer staging/canary; verify observability dashboards and alerts.
5) Deploy runtime workers with low weight; increase gradually.
6) Monitor KPIs for 48 hours; if stable, cutover remaining traffic.
7) Post-upgrade: tag TF state, archive plan outputs, and create postmortem if any incident.

Operator commands (examples):
- terraform workspace select prod-canary || terraform workspace new prod-canary
- ./scripts/tfstate-migrate.sh --from modules/legacy --to modules/private/v3 --dry-run
- kubectl drain node <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
- curl -sS -X POST "https://host/admin/migrate?step=apply" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"

Notes and open questions (to resolve before first customer cutover):
- Confirm whether customers using local installers can mirror our registry automatically or require tarball images.
- Decide SLA for how long we keep v2 control plane available for rollback.
- Finalize naming strategy for resource renames that avoid costly state moves.

Appendix: quick mapping examples (for operator reference):
- legacy module: module "runtime_pool" -> new module: module "runtime_pool_v3" (variables: keep "pool_size" alias to "replicas").
- terraform state mv example: terraform state mv module.runtime_pool.aws_autoscaling_group.asg module.runtime_pool_v3.aws_autoscaling_group.asg

Intended next steps:
- Peer-review this doc with Diego and Priya, produce a shorter customer-facing checklist, and run a dry migration in lab by 2025-02-24.
- Create CI job that validates tf-mod-v3 against a canonical lab topology nightly and fails on drift.

End of draft.
